result.summary: Fix a memory leak when spawning subprocesses on Windows by passing `std::string::data()` directly to `CreateProcessA` instead of heap-allocating a copy. This eliminates an undeleted `new[]` buffer allocation in `Popen::execute_process()`.
result.problem: On Windows, every invocation of a subprocess dynamically allocates a command line buffer using `new[]` that is never freed, leaking memory. In practice, this affects Windows nodes using `-signer=<cmd>` whenever an external signer subprocess is executed via RPC or the GUI.
evidence: PR description: "Popen::execute_process() copied the command line into a buffer from new[], but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows."
PR description notes this was also fixed upstream in arun11299/cpp-subprocess#131.
result.card: Fixes a memory leak in Windows subprocess execution where Popen::execute_process() allocated a command line buffer using new[] without deleting it. The fix passes std::string::data() directly to CreateProcessA, removing the temporary allocation entirely. The leak affects Windows nodes configured with an external signer (-signer=<cmd>) on each signer invocation, though impact is limited by the invocation rate and small command size.

risk.why: A mistake in passing the mutable string buffer could corrupt the command line arguments or cause external process execution to fail on Windows.
